reports.title: Traité portant création d'un Observatoire Economique et Statistique d'Afrique Subsaharienne (AFRISTAT)
reports.publisher: Governments of the 14 founding signatory states
reports.description: AFRISTAT's founding treaty. Independently re-fetched and confirmed this round, not just taken from Grok: "Le traité portant création d'AFRISTAT a été signé le 21 septembre 1993 à Abidjan (Côte d'Ivoire)" by fourteen founding states (Bénin, Burkina Faso, Cameroun, Centrafrique, Comores, Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Gabon, Guinée Équatoriale, Mali, Niger, Sénégal, Tchad, Togo). Also independently re-fetched: AFRISTAT's own history page confirms eight later accessions (Guinée-Bissau and Mauritanie, both 1998; Guinée, 2000; Cabo Verde, 2002; Burundi, 2006; Sao Tomé et Principe, 2008; Djibouti, 2010; Madagascar, 2013), for 22 member states total — corrects a prior secondary-sourced figure of 18 already sitting in this corpus's `ke-social-protection.json` description of AFRISTAT's role (that figure came from a 2012 UNECA presentation; this treaty and history page are AFRISTAT's own primary text and are newer/more authoritative). Left isolated: nothing found this round cites the TREATY document itself as an input — countries and CPI bulletins cite the INSTITUTION (AFRISTAT) or its methodology GUIDE (already minted as afristat-ihpc-guide-2014), not this founding instrument by name.

reports.title: Índice Nacional Harmonizado de Preços no Consumidor (INHPC) para os Países Membros da UEMOA — Guiné-Bissau
reports.description: UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23, verified methodology + named-region coverage from the January 2025 edition, downloaded and parsed directly with pdfplumber this round): the bulletin's own "Informações preliminares" section states "Este índice é considerado harmonizado porque é utilizado de acordo com a metodologia comum, adotada em 1996 pelos oito países membros da União Económica e Monetária da África Ocidental (UEMOA), porém sucessivas renovações de base foram feitas, em 2008, 2014 e 2023." It further names the CPI's actual reference-population coverage: "A população de referência do INHPC é constituída por todos os agregados familiares residentes em Bissau, e nas regiões de Gabú, Bafatá e Cacheu. O cabaz atual inclui 745 produtos monitorizados em 3489 postos de vendas a nível nacional...", and a Tabela 4 footnote identifies the basket classification as "NCOA: Nomenclatura de Consomo Oeste Africana" (the West African regional adaptation of COICOP). Page 8 also carries "Tabela 3: Preços médio a kg ou a litro de alguns produtos essências a nível regional", a price table disaggregated by the same four named areas (Bissau, Gabú, Bafatá, Cacheu) — i.e. INE itself publishes region-disaggregated price data. Original description follows. Guinea-Bissau's monthly harmonized CPI, closing the one WAEMU country left open after rounds 1-2. Per Grok's fetch (URL and quote provided, not independently re-opened this round given the site's known intermittent robots-blocking to this session's own fetch tool): "O Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INE) disponibiliza aos utilizadores o Índice Nacional Harmonizado de Preços no Consumidor (INHPC)" — title page names it explicitly as being "PARA OS PAÍSES MEMBROS DA UEMOA," base year 2023.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; example cited is the January 2025 edition.

reports.title: Índice de Precios de Consumo (IPC) — Informe Mensual
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística de Guinea Ecuatorial (INEGE)
reports.description: Distinct from gq-inege-anuario-2024 (the annual statistical yearbook, minted in af-cemac.json): a dedicated monthly inflation/IPC report. Per Grok's fetch: "TASA DE INFLACIÓN ÍNDICE DE PRECIOS DE CONSUMO … El mes de febrero de 2026 registra una tasa de inflación de 2,4%." Resolves this branch's round-3 deferred lead ("gq-inege-anuario-2024 -> cemac-ihpc-regulation", reason: deferred) by supplying the correct, narrower node the CEMAC hub should actually connect to instead of the broad yearbook.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; example cited is the February 2026 edition, confirming the series is current as of this year.

reports.title: Règlement N°04/21-UEAC-115-CM-36 portant modalités d'élaboration, de calcul et de diffusion de l'inflation sous-jacente
reports.publisher: CEMAC (Communauté Économique et Monétaire de l'Afrique Centrale)
reports.description: The companion regulation to cemac-ihpc-regulation, both named on the same page (5) of CEMAC's own 2024 inflation note: "la Commission de la CEMAC a adopté le Règlement N°04/21-UEAC-115-CM-36 portant modalités d'élaboration, de calcul et de diffusion de l'inflation sous-jacente au sein des États membres." Its own primary full text was not located by Grok or by this session — only this describing passage in the same secondary source already used for cemac-ihpc-regulation. Minted (rather than left as a dropped lead) because the quote is specific and the source is the same primary CEMAC Commission document already trusted for the sibling regulation; flagged honestly that this is a title/date/description, not a self-standing primary read.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (a supranational regulation), same shape as cemac-ihpc-regulation.

reports.title: Indice des Prix à la Consommation des ménages au Burundi
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique du Burundi (INSBU; successor branding to ISTEEBU)
reports.description: Burundi's monthly CPI, closing the EAC-member gap flagged in G.15. Per Grok's fetch: "Institut National de la Statistique du Burundi … Indice des Prix à la Consommation des ménages au Burundi Mois d'avril 2026 … Le taux d'inflation mensuel s'établit à +3,0% en avril 2026." Note the institution rebranded from ISTEEBU (the name used in this branch's prior G.15 lead) to INSBU — worth remembering if a future session searches under the old name and finds nothing.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; example cited is April 2026, confirming the series is current.

reports.title: South Sudan Consumer Price Index
reports.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), South Sudan
reports.description: South Sudan's monthly CPI. Per Grok's fetch: "South Sudan Consumer Price Index for May 2025 National Bureau of Statistics … The Index covers the ten states of South Sudan." Closes one of the three previously-unresearched EAC members flagged in G.15.

reports.title: Somalia Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.description: Somalia's CPI, independently re-fetched and confirmed this round. Verbatim, own methodological note: a "comprehensive modernization of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) system" completed with World Bank technical support, adopting COICOP 2018, expanding "geographic coverage to all Federal Member States and Somaliland," reweighted from the 2022 SIHBS survey. Framed here as a MODERNIZATION with expanded coverage, not literally Somalia's first-ever CPI as Grok's original framing suggested ("the first nationally representative CPI") — the methodological note itself says the modernization achieved nationally representative status, implying an earlier, more limited-coverage series existed before May 2025. Monthly cadence confirmed by recent release titles (e.g. "Consumer Price Index (CPI) June 2026").
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, confirmed current as of June 2026 per a recently-published release title.

reports.title: African Charter on Statistics
reports.description: The Charter (adopted 2009) is now mintable for the first time: Tanzania's own Statistics Act, Cap. 351 (R.E. 2023), Section 3 (Interpretation), independently re-fetched and confirmed this round, defines "international standards" verbatim as "standards or guidelines for producing statistical information prescribed in the African Charter on Statistics, 2009, the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics of the United Nations, other standards issued by recognised international organisations and includes international best practices." This is a national statute naming the Charter directly by title and year — the first documented case in this corpus of an AF-branch country's own law citing it, closing G.15's open lead. Parallel checks of South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, Ethiopia and Egypt's statistics acts did not surface an equally clear citation this round (per Grok) — not independently re-checked by this session; a real gap, not a confirmed absence for those six.

reports.title: The Statistics Act, Cap. 351 (Revised Edition 2023)
reports.description: Tanzania's Statistics Act, the statute whose Section 3 (Interpretation) names the African Charter on Statistics as one basis for "international standards" — see african-charter-statistics-2009 above for the verbatim quote. Not previously in this corpus; minted specifically to carry that edge.

_dropped.edge: SADC Protocol on Statistics -> ratification status (Botswana, Zambia)
_dropped.why: Grok reported, quoting French, that a 30 May 2025 SADC press release states the Statistics Committee "a félicité la République du Botswana et la République de Zambie d'avoir ratifié le protocole sur les statistiques." This session independently re-fetched the SAME URL Grok cited (both the English original and a French wire-service syndication of the same event, https://fr.apanews.net/integration/sadc-appel-pressant-a-ratifier-le-protocole-sur-les-statistiques/) and searched specifically for "Botswana" and "Zambia"/"Zambie": neither name appears anywhere in either article body (Botswana appears only in SADC's postal-address footer). Both independently-fetched versions describe ratification as still pending, with the Committee only having "received reports from Member States on the progress that they have made." This is a genuine discrepancy between Grok's answer and this session's own re-check of the identical source — recorded here rather than silently accepted or silently dropped, per Thomas's own instruction to double-check recency and accuracy. Not treated as confirmed. The SADC Protocol's ratification status remains open; a 30 May 2025 meeting report exists and is real, but the specific Botswana/Zambia claim could not be reproduced from it.
